design_rules: F2 defines learning destinations and spatial architecture only; it contains no polished story prose and does not release Unit 8 to students.
All 255 F1 canonical records remain unchanged; F2 assigns learning function without editing scientific content.
Behavior loci keep proximate/ultimate, innate/learned, sign-stimulus/response, kinesis/taxis, and fitness explanations explicitly discriminable.
Energy flows one way through ecosystems while matter cycles; no locus may imply that organisms create energy or that energy is recycled.
Biogeochemical-cycle loci must encode reservoirs and process direction, especially the distinct nitrogen transformations.
Population equations must keep dN/dt, N, B, D, rmax, and K distinct; equation symbols remain visually attached to their biological meanings.
Exponential and logistic models remain idealized models with explicit assumptions; carrying capacity is environment-dependent and not permanently fixed.
r- and K-selection remain ends of a life-history continuum, not rigid organism types.
Community loci must keep habitat/niche, fundamental/realized niche, and interaction-sign distinctions visible.
Simpson diversity index must use the AP equation 1 − Σ(n/N)² with n and N visibly distinguished and larger values interpreted as greater diversity for this form.
Keystone and foundation species remain distinct and context-dependent.
Introduced does not automatically mean invasive, and mutation is never represented as directed by environmental need.
Biological magnification, eutrophication, ocean acidification, habitat fragmentation, and overharvesting remain distinct mechanisms rather than a generic human-impact category.
Every permanent locus requires a scientific visual in addition to any later mnemonic or narrative imagery.

journeys.content_focus: Behavioral and physiological response, communication, learning, movement, reproductive/social behavior, and plant environmental response
journeys.setting_logic: A research institute uses stable analysis stations so cause, cue, response, learning mode, movement direction, communication, and fitness consequences remain physically distinguishable.

journeys.content_focus: Organism energy budgets, thermoregulation, ecological levels, trophic roles, production, and energy transfer
journeys.setting_logic: A power-and-transfer hall follows energy from organism budgets through primary capture, trophic transfer, and ecosystem-level consequences while matter conservation remains separately visible.

bundles.title: Energy budgets, thermoregulation, and ecosystem frame

journeys.content_focus: Matter reservoirs, transfer processes, and the water, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles
journeys.setting_logic: A watershed-scale map gives each major cycle a distinct route while a common reservoir-transfer station preserves the shared logic of matter cycling.

journeys.content_focus: Population density and dispersion, demographic records, survivorship, population change accounting, and life-history trade-offs
journeys.setting_logic: A field reserve moves from counting where organisms are, through age-specific survival records, to population-change accounting and lifetime allocation patterns.

journeys.content_focus: Exponential and logistic growth models, carrying capacity, and density-dependent versus density-independent regulation
journeys.setting_logic: A model-control center places each growth equation beside its graph and assumptions, then routes populations through separate density-dependent and density-independent regulation panels.

journeys.content_focus: Community, habitat and niche, interspecific interactions, competition, predation, symbiosis, disturbance, and succession
journeys.setting_logic: A shared ecological district separates spatial habitat from functional niche, then uses interaction zones and post-disturbance sites to make species effects and succession physically traceable.

bundles.title: Community structure, niches, and interaction signs

journeys.content_focus: Species diversity measurement, Simpson diversity index, biodiversity, resilience, keystone effects, and foundation species
journeys.setting_logic: An observatory first measures composition quantitatively, then tests how different forms of diversity and disproportionately influential species affect community response.

journeys.content_focus: Adaptation, biological invasions, habitat change, overharvesting, pollution, eutrophication, ocean acidification, and large-scale environmental drivers
journeys.setting_logic: A response center traces distinct environmental-change mechanisms to population/community consequences and prevents separate mechanisms from collapsing into a generic human-impact story.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Proximate versus ultimate causation
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Distinguish immediate mechanism/development from evolutionary function/history.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Innate versus learned behavior
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Classify how prior experience contributes to the basic response without assuming all behavior is purely one or the other.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Fixed action pattern versus sign stimulus
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate the patterned response from the cue that triggers it.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Kinesis versus taxis
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate non-directional change in activity/turning from directed movement relative to a stimulus.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Phototaxis versus phototropism
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate whole-organism directed movement from directional plant growth.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Signal versus pheromone
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Treat pheromone as one chemical signal type, not as a synonym for every signal.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Imprinting versus other learned behavior
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Identify sensitive-period learning without applying imprinting to every persistent learned response.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Polygyny versus polyandry
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Keep the sex of the individual with multiple mates explicit.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Cooperation versus altruism
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate broadly cooperative outcomes from the direct-fitness cost required by the behavioral-ecology definition of altruism.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Kin selection versus inclusive fitness
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate the selection process from the fitness accounting that includes effects on relatives.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Endotherm versus ectotherm
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Distinguish predominant heat source without claiming either group has constant versus variable body temperature by definition.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Biotic versus abiotic factor
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate living/biological components from nonliving physical and chemical components.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Energy flow versus matter cycling
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Energy ultimately leaves as heat while matter is conserved and cycles among reservoirs.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Autotroph versus heterotroph
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Distinguish carbon/energy acquisition modes.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Producer, consumer, decomposer roles
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Discriminate trophic roles from trophic-level numbering alone.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Food chain versus food web
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate a simplified linear pathway from interconnected feeding relationships and retain arrow direction.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: GPP, NPP, and secondary production
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Keep total producer production, producer production after respiration, and new heterotroph biomass distinct.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Major biogeochemical cycles
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Identify the dominant reservoirs and transformations for water, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Nitrogen-cycle transformations
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Discriminate chemical direction and biological role of fixation, ammonification, nitrification, denitrification, and assimilation.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Population, community, ecosystem, biome
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Keep ecological levels nested and do not collapse population/community/ecosystem.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Population density versus dispersion
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate number per area/volume from spatial arrangement.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Clumped, uniform, and random dispersion
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Classify spatial pattern while holding density conceptually separate.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Life table versus survivorship curve
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate tabulated age/stage survival data from its graphical survivorship representation.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Type I, II, and III survivorship
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Distinguish the age-specific mortality shapes rather than memorizing example species.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Absolute population growth versus per-capita rate
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Keep dN/dt distinct from a rate scaled to N and interpret rmax as a per-capita parameter in the exponential model.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Exponential versus logistic growth
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Select the model from assumptions and resource limitation, then connect equation to graph.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: rmax versus K
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate intrinsic maximum per-capita growth parameter from carrying capacity.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Density-dependent versus density-independent
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Determine whether per-capita effect changes systematically with density.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Habitat versus ecological niche
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate where an organism lives from how it uses resources/conditions and interacts.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Fundamental versus realized niche
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate potential niche from the portion occupied under biotic constraints.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Competition, predation, and symbiosis
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Discriminate interaction mechanism and fitness signs.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Batesian versus Müllerian mimicry
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate a harmless/palatable mimic of a defended model from convergence among defended species.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Parasitism, mutualism, and commensalism
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Use +/−, +/+, and +/0 effects without assuming every close association is mutualism.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Primary versus secondary succession
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Use soil and biological legacy status as the key distinction.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Species richness, relative abundance, and species diversity
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate number of species, proportional composition, and the combined diversity concept.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Simpson n versus N
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Keep species-specific count n distinct from total community-sample count N.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Keystone versus foundation species
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate disproportionate effect relative to abundance from habitat-forming/high-abundance influence.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Introduced versus invasive species
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Introduction outside historical range is insufficient by itself for the invasive label.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Biological magnification versus eutrophication
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Separate trophic concentration of persistent substances from nutrient-driven production/decomposition and oxygen decline.

mixed_discrimination_sets.title: Mutation and adaptation causal order
mixed_discrimination_sets.purpose: Variation arises without need-directed mutation; selection changes frequencies of variants under environmental conditions.
